title: Turn a revoked Google grant from a silent 'unavailable' into Reconnect now
deviations_from_card: Write set shrunk by nothing, grown by nothing: 15 card files + grant-health.test.ts + the existing calendar-status-i18n.test.ts (named in the card's acceptance). 'undecryptable' does NOT short-circuit (decrypt is local, no network) and heals back to 'ok' when the key returns; only 'revoked' stops all calls. Health lives as two nullable columns on calendar_connections (idempotent ALTER in token-store db(); the table is already in the tenancy manifest and the new UPDATE filters workspace_id, so tenancy.ts untouched). The unbacked 'operator sees a disconnected integration' comment in google-calendar.ts is replaced with what actually happens. Catalog keys: scheduleTab.lifecycle.calendarStatus.needs_reconnect + integrations.calendar.grant.{revokedTitle,revokedBody,undecryptableTitle,undecryptableBody,unsynced,reconnectAction}. unsyncedUpcoming is 0 when no connection row exists.
notes: Test commit 92161b9b5 is red by design (tests-first); the catalog (0473c5ccd) and doc (cab80ee28) commits went in alone under the lock, green from e90e1613b. tsc exit 2 ONLY on untracked kpi-sim/runs/** (foreign); zero errors in the tree proper, recorded as 0. Touched-dir unit tests: 620/620 green (calendar, schedule*, tenancy*, schedule + calendar routes, integrations + schedule features, api contracts). Full npm run test:unit failures are all foreign: recipes-literals ratchet on features/hiring/channels/ChannelsReceiverPullCard.tsx (candidate-channels-ui sibling), devcase-studio-robustness + devcase-candidate-refusals (devcase sibling).
